ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.claim: People who assume descent from Abraham and Moses entitles them to Paradise are condemned; Islahi redirects attention to those prophets' teachings and sacrifices.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p40/r6.anchor: Their attention is directed to the teachings and sacrifices of these prophets

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r5.claim: The verses portray miserly people who give little, yet presume a high rank in the Hereafter; Islahi asks whether they can see the unseen to know their promised status.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r5.anchor: Do they have a telescope which is capable of seeing the matters of the unseen world

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.speaker: our exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.claim: Exegetes generally identify the person in the passage as Walīd ibn al-Mughīrah, a Quraysh chief, and recount his abandoned plan to embrace Islam.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p63/r6.anchor: Our exegetes generally regard ﻟﺬيۡ to be a reference to Wal īd ibn al-Mughīrah

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.speaker: our exegetes
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.claim: Exegetes report that a companion promised to shield Walīd from the Hereafter if he paid money; Walīd abandoned conversion, promised payment, then paid only part.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r1.anchor: Though this incident has been cited by all our exegetes,

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.claim: Islahi says the report has no sound chain and, even if true, its connection to these verses is unclear; the Qur’an is not rebuking Walīd for breaking a promise.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r2.anchor: in the first place it does not have a sound chain of narration, and if it is supposed that this incident is true

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.claim: He criticizes exegetes for treating the generic relative al-ladhī or al as a proper noun, then inventing a person and an ill-fitting incident to explain it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r3.anchor: they start looking for a person whom these words qualify.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.claim: The relative forms al-ladhī and al can also introduce a parable that portrays a group’s collective character through a specific figure.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r4.anchor: at certain instances, they are used to portray a parable too. At such instances, the purpose is to present the collective character of a group

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.claim: The woman in 16:92 who unravels her spun thread is a symbolic example, not a particular old woman whose identity and biography need investigation.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r5.anchor: it does not refer to a specific old lady so that one may start investigating her name, family and whereabouts

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.claim: A hypothetical miserly idolater represents Arabs who refuse to spend yet expect Paradise through alleged deities and racial superiority; Walīd, Abū Jahl, and other wealthy Quraysh see themselves in it.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r6.anchor: a hypothetical character is portrayed to the Idolaters of Arabia.

ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.author: Amin Ahsan Islahi (d. 1997)
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.speaker: author
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.claim: The discourse uses disparaging, sarcastic irony toward people who give grudgingly yet act as if they can already see Paradise’s luxuries.
ISLAHI-TADABBUR:vol-8-english:p64/r7.anchor: The style of the discourse in these verses is disparaging and sarcastic:

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r15.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r15.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r15.claim: The question challenges whether he knows from the unseen that another person bearing his sins would benefit him, and thus sees the truth with insight, or whether he is ignorant.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r15.anchor: أعنده علم الغيب: أي أعلم من الغيب أن من تحمل ذنوب آخر، فإنه المتحمل عنه ينتفع بذلك

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r16.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r16.speaker: الزمخشري
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r16.claim: Al-Zamakhshari says he knows that his brother's promise to bear his burdens is true.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r16.anchor: وقال الزمخشري: فهو يرى: فهو يعلم أن ما قاله أخوه من احتمال أوزاره حق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r17.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r17.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p22/r17.claim: Another view says he knows his own condition in the afterlife.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r1.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r1.speaker: الزجاج
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r1.claim: Al-Zajjaj takes “he sees” to mean that he sees his sin lifted in the afterlife.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r1.anchor: وقال الزجاج: يرى رفع مأثمه في الآخرة

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r2.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r2.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r2.claim: An alternative says he sees that what he heard from the Qurʾan is false.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r2.anchor: وقيل: فهو يرى أن ما سمعه من القرآن باطل

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r3.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r3.speaker: الكلبي
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi says revelation came to him, and he then saw that what had been withheld from him was true.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي: أنزل عليه قرآن، فرأى ما منعه حق

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r4.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r4.speaker: قيل
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r4.claim: A brief alternative gloss reads “he sees” as referring to the parts.

ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r5.author: Abū Ḥayyān al-Gharnāṭī
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r5.speaker: author
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r5.claim: The verb may mean literal sight of what is hidden from others, or knowledge of the unseen as one knows what is witnessed.
ABUHAYYAN-FULL:v10p23/r5.anchor: واحتمل يرى أن تكون بصرية، أي فهو يبصر ما خفي عن غيره مما هو غيب، واحتمل أن يكون بمعنى يعلم

STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.claim: The third section calls people to reflect on their creation and transitions to enduring truths in the scriptures of Moses and Abraham.
STUDYQURAN:53:intro/r16.anchor: the third section (vv. 31–54) calls upon people to reflect upon their creation

RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r4.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r4.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r4.claim: The question about unseen knowledge answers 53:30: the man's limited worldly knowledge is no knowledge of the unseen or of the afterlife.
RAZI-FULL:v29p11/r4.anchor: أي لم يعلم الغيب وما في الآخرة

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r5.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r5.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r5.claim: The question exposes the turner's ignorance and need, and the ugliness of turning away when he ought to heed; unseen knowledge is knowledge of what is hidden from creatures.
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r5.anchor: المراد جهل المتولي وحاجته وبيان قبح التولي مع الحاجة إلى الإقبال

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r6.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r6.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r6.claim: Seeing would excuse turning away only when the unseen is directly visible, at the time faith no longer benefits; until then a person needs the guide who leads toward a destination not yet seen.
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r6.anchor: تتمة بيان وقت جواز التولي وهو حصول الرؤية وهو الوقت الذي لا ينفع الإيمان فيه

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r7.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r7.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r7.claim: One possible object of يرى is the belief that one person's burden is carried by another: the man supposes this while unaware that each bears only his own.

RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r8.author: Fakhr al-Dīn al-Rāzī
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r8.speaker: author
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r8.claim: Alternatively, يرى has no expressed object and means that the man sees his own judgment as sufficient, needing neither guide nor warner.
RAZI-FULL:v29p11#2/r8.anchor: ويحتمل أن لا يكون له مفعول تقديره فهو يرى رأي نظر غير محتاج إلى هاد ونذير

STUDYQURAN:53:35/r1.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:35/r1.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:35/r1.claim: In context, the verse asks whether the man who stopped giving charity knows his earlier deeds suffice or that his wealth will remain safe if he withholds charity.
STUDYQURAN:53:35/r1.anchor: Does the one who stopped giving charity know that his past deeds will suffice or that his wealth will actually be preserved if he does not give it out in charity?

STUDYQURAN:53:35/r2.author: Seyyed Hossein Nasr (ed.-in-chief), Caner K. Dagli, Maria Massi Dakake, Joseph E. B. Lumbard, Mohammed Rustom
STUDYQURAN:53:35/r2.speaker: author
STUDYQURAN:53:35/r2.claim: More broadly, it criticizes the arrogance of people acting as if they know better than God.
STUDYQURAN:53:35/r2.anchor: In the broader Quranic context, it indicates the arrogance of those who act as if they know better than God; see 52:41; 68:47.

BURSEVI:v9p201/r1.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r1.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201/r1.claim: The fāʾ marks consequence and seeing is inward knowledge: does he know the unseen, including whether his companion's punishment can be borne by another?
BURSEVI:v9p201/r1.anchor: الفاء للسببية والرؤية قلبية أي أعنده علم بالأمور الغيبية التي من جملتها تحمل صاحبه عنه يوم القيامة

BURSEVI:v9p201/r2.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r2.speaker: ابن الشيخ
BURSEVI:v9p201/r2.claim: Ibn al-Shaykh reads arāʾayta as 'informed'; the question about unseen knowledge is its second object, while yarā means 'knows' with both objects omitted from context.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r2.anchor: قال ابن الشيخ : أرأت بمعنى أخبرت وأعنده علم الغيب مفعوله الثاني

BURSEVI:v9p201/r3.author: İsmāʿīl Ḥaqqī Bursevī
BURSEVI:v9p201/r3.speaker: author
BURSEVI:v9p201/r3.claim: The alternative asks whether he is ignorant, never having been told what is in Moses' scrolls, meaning the books of the Torah.
BURSEVI:v9p201/r3.anchor: {أم} أهو جاهل {لم ينبأ} لم يخبر {بما فى صحف موسى} أي أسفار التوراة

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r9.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r9.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r9.claim: The pronouns refer to the person who turned away, and the question is a repudiation.

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r10.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r10.speaker: المفسرون
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r10.claim: The reported interpretation asks whether he knows the unseen well enough to know that his companion will bear his sins and suffer punishment in his place if he deserves it.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r10.anchor: والاستفهام للإنكار والمعنى أيعلم الغيب فيترتب عليه أن يعلم أن صاحبه يتحمل عنه ذنوبه ويعذب مكانه يوم القيامة لو استحق العذاب. كذا فسروا

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r11.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r11.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r11.claim: Al-Tabatabai instead takes the unseen to mean the future course of worldly life: did he know that continued spending would exhaust his wealth and leave him poor?
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r11.anchor: والظاهر أن المراد نفي علمه بما غاب عنه من مستقبل حاله في الدنيا

TABATABAI:53:33-37/r12.author: Muḥammad Ḥusayn al-Ṭabāṭabāʾī
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r12.speaker: author
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r12.claim: The claim that someone else will carry his sins is addressed by the next statement that no bearer carries another’s burden.
TABATABAI:53:33-37/r12.anchor: وأما تحمل الذنوب والعذاب فالمتعرض له قوله الآتي { أن لا تزر وازرة وزر أخرى }

TABRISI:53:32-39/r12.author: al-Ṭabrisī
TABRISI:53:32-39/r12.speaker: author
TABRISI:53:32-39/r12.claim: The unseen matter at issue is the punishment: does the miser know and see that another person will bear his punishment for him?
TABRISI:53:32-39/r12.anchor: أي ما غاب عنه من أمر العذاب

THALABI:v9p151/r7.author: al-Thaʿlabī
THALABI:v9p151/r7.speaker: author
THALABI:v9p151/r7.claim: The question asks whether he possesses knowledge of the unseen and therefore sees for himself; yunabbaʾ means ‘be informed.’
THALABI:v9p151/r7.anchor: أعنده علم الغيب فهو يرى أم لم ينبأ يخبر بما في صحف موسى

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65/r1.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65/r1.speaker: author
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65/r1.claim: The unseen in question is the punishment, and the man supposes his companion will bear it for him.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65/r1.anchor: يعني ما غاب عنه من أمر العذاب

WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65/r2.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65/r2.speaker: الزجاج
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65/r2.claim: Al-Zajjāj takes seeing as knowing; one can say of a blind person, “I saw Zayd as intelligent,” and the man would claim knowledge that another bears his punishment.
WAHIDI-BASIT:v21p65/r2.anchor: قال الزجاج: (فهو يرى) معناه فهو يعلم، والرؤية تكون بمعنى العلم

WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r7.author: al-Wāḥidī
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r7.speaker: author
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r7.claim: The rebuke asks whether he has unseen knowledge of the Hereafter that lets him know someone else will carry his punishment.
WAHIDI-WAJIZ:53:32-35/r7.anchor: ما غاب عنه من أمر الآخرة، حتى علم أن غيره يحمل عنه العذاب

ELMALILI:53:33-54/r3.author: Elmalılı Muhammed Hamdi Yazır
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r3.speaker: author
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r3.claim: The question challenges whether he can see the unseen and thus knows that someone else will carry his afterlife burden.
ELMALILI:53:33-54/r3.anchor: Şimdiden âhireti görüyor da günahını başkasının yüklenivereceğini biliyor mu?

KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.author: Hayreddin Karaman, Mustafa Çağrıcı, İbrahim Kâfi Dönmez, Sadrettin Gümüş
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.speaker: author
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.claim: Tafsīr reports connect these verses with episodes showing some polytheists’ fickle conduct, but the reports are unreliable and their narrative details sit uneasily with Qur’anic principles.
KURANYOLU-TEFSIR:53:33/r1.anchor: bunların sağlam haberler olmadığı anlaşılmaktadır; ayrıca olayların kurgusunda Kur’an’ın ilkelerine göre izahı kolay olmayan unsurlar bulunmaktadır

BURHAN:v3p171/r5.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p171/r5.speaker: الفارسي
BURHAN:v3p171/r5.claim: Al-Fārisī takes ‘yarā’ as governing two omitted objects: seeing the unseen means knowing it, as though the unseen were present; he links this to ‘Knower of the unseen.’
BURHAN:v3p171/r5.anchor: قال الفارسي الوجه أن يرى هنا للتعدية لمفعولين لأن رؤية الغائب لا تكون إلا علما

BURHAN:v3p171/r6.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p171/r6.speaker: ابن خروف
BURHAN:v3p171/r6.claim: Ibn Khurūf says the two objects are omitted with contextual evidence: the person knows what he does and believes it true and right.
BURHAN:v3p171/r6.anchor: وقال ابن خروف هو من باب الحذف لدليل لأن المعنى دال على المفعولين

BURHAN:v3p171/r7.author: al-Zarkashī
BURHAN:v3p171/r7.speaker: author
BURHAN:v3p171/r7.claim: The author rejects the analysis that leaves the objects wholly unspecified: it gives the verse no determinate meaning, despite some scholars adopting it.
BURHAN:v3p171/r7.anchor: ولا فائدة في الآية مع الاقتصار لأنه لا يعلم منه المراد وقد ذهب إليه بعض المحققين وعدل عن الصواب

ITQAN:v2p563#2/r4.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p563#2/r4.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p563#2/r4.claim: The Qur'an uses plural winds in contexts of mercy and singular wind in contexts of punishment.
ITQAN:v2p563#2/r4.anchor: فحيث ذكرت في سياق الرحمة جمعت أو في سياق العذاب أفردت

ITQAN:v2p563#2/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p563#2/r5.speaker: أبي بن كعب
ITQAN:v2p563#2/r5.claim: Ubayy ibn Kaʿb reports that every Qur'anic plural form of winds denotes mercy and every singular form denotes punishment; Ibn Abi Hatim and others transmit the report.
ITQAN:v2p563#2/r5.anchor: عن أبي بن كعب قال كل شيء في القرآن من الرياح فهو رحمة وكل شيء فيه من الريح فهو عذاب

ITQAN:v2p563#2/r6.author: al-Suyūṭī
ITQAN:v2p563#2/r6.speaker: author
ITQAN:v2p563#2/r6.claim: The source cites a prophetic prayer asking for winds rather than a single wind, and explains that merciful winds vary and temper one another, whereas punitive wind arrives from one unopposed direction.
ITQAN:v2p563#2/r6.anchor: ورد في الحديث اللهم اجعلها رياحا ولا تجعلها ريحا وذكر في حكمة ذلك أن رياح الرحمة مختلفة الصفات

DAMGHANI:v1p332/r17.author: al-Dāmghānī
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r17.speaker: author
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r17.claim: ʿIndahu can mean does he know; the question asks whether he knows the unseen.
DAMGHANI:v1p332/r17.anchor: اعنده اي العلم قوله سبحانه في سورة النجم اعنده علم الغيب اي ايعلم علم الغيب

IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#4/r1.author: Ibn Qutayba
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#4/r1.speaker: author
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#4/r1.claim: The question asks whether he knows the unseen, including the affairs of the Hereafter, and so can see them.
IBNQUTAYBA-GHARIB:v1p429#4/r1.anchor: {أعنده علم الغيب فهو يرى} أي يعرف ما غاب عنه: من أمر الآخرة وغيرها؟!

NAHHAS:v4p274/r16.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r16.speaker: سيبويه
NAHHAS:v4p274/r16.claim: Sibawayh transmits that yarā here means knows.

NAHHAS:v4p274/r17.author: Abū Jaʿfar al-Naḥḥās
NAHHAS:v4p274/r17.speaker: author
NAHHAS:v4p274/r17.claim: The question challenges whether the man knows the unseen well enough to see that another person can bear his punishment.
NAHHAS:v4p274/r17.anchor: أي أعلم أن هذا يتحمل عنه العذاب كما قال ويرى بمعنى يعلم

SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r1.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r1.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r1.claim: The question أعنده علم الغيب is the second object of أعطى; its first object is omitted for concision.
SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r1.anchor: و { أعنده علم }: هو المفعول الثاني. والمفعول الأول محذوف اقتصارا لأعطى.

SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r2.author: al-Samīn al-Ḥalabī
SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r2.speaker: author
SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r2.claim: فهو يرى follows plainly as a nominal clause; Abu al-Baqa instead makes it stand for a verb, فيرى, which would be subjunctive as an answer to the question, but the author finds that unnecessary.
SAMIN-DURR:53:35/r2.anchor: وهذا لا حاجة إليه مع ظهور الترتب بالجملة الاسمية، وقد تقدم له نظير هذا الكلام

ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r3.author: al-Zajjāj
ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r3.speaker: author
ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r3.claim: Seeing can mean physical sight or knowing; a blind person saying he sees Zayd as intelligent cannot mean sight by eye.
ZAJJAJ:v5p74#2/r3.anchor: ألا ترى أن المكفوف يقول: رأيت زيدا عاقلا، فلو كان من رؤية العين لم يجز

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r1.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r1.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r1.claim: The fa introduces a consequence of the preceding question: does he possess unseen knowledge, and therefore know his companion will bear his burden at Judgment?
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r1.anchor: والفاء في قوله تعالى : ( فهو يرى ( للتسبب عما قبله أي أعنده علم بالأمور الغيبية

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r2.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r2.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r2.claim: One possible sense is that he sees what he heard from the Qur'an as false.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r2.anchor: وقيل : يرى أن ما سمعه من القرآن باطل

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r3.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r3.speaker: الكلبي
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r3.claim: Al-Kalbi takes the question to mean: was a Qur'an sent down to him, so that he judged his conduct right?
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r3.anchor: وقال الكلبي : المعنى أأنزل عليه قرآن فرأى أن ما صنعه حق

ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r4.author: al-Ālūsī
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r4.speaker: author
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r4.claim: The verb most readily describes inward perception, though it may also mean physical sight of what is hidden from others.
ALUSI-FULL:v27p65#3/r4.anchor: وأيا ما كان فيرى من الرؤية القلبية وجوز أن تكون من الرؤية البصرية

BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r1.author: al-Baghawī
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r1.speaker: author
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r1.claim: The question challenges whether he knows the unseen and can see that his companion will bear his punishment.
BAGHAWI-FULL:v7p414#2/r1.anchor: ما غاب عنه ويعلم أن صاحبه يتحمل عنه عذابه

BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r5.author: al-Bayḍāwī
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r5.speaker: author
BAYDAWI-FULL:53:33-35/r5.claim: The rebuke asks whether he knows the unseen and can see that his partner will bear the punishment for him.

BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r6.author: al-Biqāʿī
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r6.speaker: author
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r6.claim: The question rebukes the claim that he possesses all unseen knowledge and can therefore foresee every benefit and harm, know what God accepts, and judge his small donation sufficient.
BIQAI-FULL:v7p329/r6.anchor: أعنده } أي خاصة { علم الغيب } أي كله بحيث لا يشاركه في مشارك يمكن أن يخفى عليه شيء منه { فهو } أي فيتسبب عن ذلك أنه { يرى * }

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.speaker: ابن زيد
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.claim: Ibn Zayd says the verses concern a new Muslim who feared God but was offered relief from all punishment by an opponent if he paid; he paid a little, then bargained, and documented the deal.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r5.anchor: عن ابن زيد قال: إن رجلا أسلم فلقيه بعض من يعيره فقال: أتركت دين الأشياخ وضللتهم وزعمت أنهم في النار

DURR-FULL:v7p658/r8.author: al-Suyūṭī
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r8.speaker: مجاهد
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r8.claim: Mujahid identifies the unseen here as the Qurʾan and asks whether al-Walid saw any falsehood in it while visiting the Prophet and Abu Bakr.
DURR-FULL:v7p658/r8.anchor: نزل في ذلك {أعنده علم الغيب} قال: الغيب القرآن أرأى فيه باطلا أنفذه ببصره

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r6.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r6.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r6.claim: The question denies he knows the unseen well enough to think hiring someone to bear his punishment will save him; it exposes his error.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r6.anchor: والاستفهام في { أعنده علم الغيب } إنكاري على توهمه أن استئجار أحد ليتحمل عنه عذاب الله

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r7.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r7.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r7.claim: This explanatory restart answers the astonishment in ‘Have you seen the one who turned away?’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r7.anchor: والجملة استئناف بياني للاستفهام التعجيبي من قوله : { أفرأيت الذي تولى }

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r8.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r8.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r8.claim: Fronting ‘with him’ emphasizes the bizarre claim that he possesses knowledge of the unseen and his distance from that status.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r8.anchor: وتقديم { عنده } وهو مسند على { علم الغيب } وهو مسند إليه للاهتمام بهذه العندية العجيب ادعاؤها

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r9.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r9.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r9.claim: Knowledge of the unseen means knowledge of hidden realms, inferred from evidence yet phrased as if witnessed, in light of ‘so he sees.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r9.anchor: وعلم الغيب : معرفة العوالم المغيبة ، أي العلم الحاصل من أدلة فكأنه شاهد الغيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r10.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r10.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r10.claim: The consequence means he sees unseen matters; yarā is visual and its omitted object is ‘the unseen.’
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r10.anchor: والرؤية في قوله : { فهو يرى } بصرية ومفعولها محذوف ، والتقدير : فهو يرى الغيب .

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.claim: He acted as though paying someone to carry the consequences of abandoning Islam would avert punishment, assuming both that turning away was a crime and that afterlife sins could be transferred.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p128/r11.anchor: والمعنى : أنه آمن نفسه من تبعة التولي عن الإسلام ببذل شيء لمن تحمل عنه تبعة توليه كأنه يعلم الغيب

IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r1.author: Ibn ʿĀshūr
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r1.speaker: author
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r1.claim: Fronting the subject pronoun over its verb strengthens the assertion that he sees, intensifying the wonder at his confidence in the bargain he made.
IBNASHUR-FULL:v27p129/r1.anchor: وتقديم الضمير المسند إليه على فعله المسند دون أن يقول : فيرى ، لإفادة تقوي الحكم ، نحو : هو يعطي الجزيل .

IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r1.author: Ibn ʿAṭiyya
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r1.speaker: author
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r1.claim: The question asks whether he knows that taking another’s burden benefits that person, or is ignorant because he was not informed.
IBNATIYYA-FULL:v5p205#2/r1.anchor: معناه: أعلم من الغيب أن من تحمل ذنوب آخر فإن المتحمل عنه ينتفع بذلك، فهو لهذا الذي علمه يرى الحق

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#2/r1.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#2/r1.speaker: الفراء
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#2/r1.claim: Al-Farrāʾ reads ‘does he see?’ as seeing his condition in the afterlife.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#2/r1.anchor: أحدهما فهو يرى حاله في الآخرة قاله الفراء

IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#2/r2.author: Ibn al-Jawzī
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#2/r2.speaker: ابن قتيبة
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#2/r2.claim: Ibn Qutaybah says it means knowing what is hidden from him, including the affairs of the afterlife and beyond.
IBNJAWZI-ZAD:v8p78#2/r2.anchor: والثاني فهو يعلم ما غاب عنه من أمر الآخرة وغيرها قاله ابن قتيبة

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r4.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r4.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r4.claim: The rhetorical question asks whether the miser knows by unseen knowledge that his money will run out and sees that outcome; plainly he does not.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r4.anchor: أي: أعند هذا الذي قد أمسك يده خشية الإنفاق، وقطع معروفه، أعنده علم الغيب أنه سينفد ما في يده

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r5.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r5.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r5.claim: He withheld charity, kindness, good works, and family ties from greed, stinginess, and alarm.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r5.anchor: وإنما أمسك عن الصدقة والمعروف والبر والصلة بخلا وشحا وهلعا

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r6.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r6.claim: A hadith urges Bilal to spend without fearing that the Lord of the Throne will make him poor.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r6.anchor: ولهذا جاء في الحديث: "أنفق بلالا ولا تخش من ذي العرش إقلالا"

IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r7.author: Ibn Kathīr
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r7.speaker: author
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r7.claim: God promises to replace whatever people spend and is the best provider, as stated in 34:39.
IBNKATHIR-FULL:v7p463/r7.anchor: وقد قال الله تعالى: {وما أنفقتم من شيء فهو يخلفه وهو خير الرازقين} [سبأ: 39]

KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r4.author: al-Zamakhsharī
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r4.speaker: author
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r4.claim: He knows his brother's promise to bear all his sins is true.
KASHSHAF-FULL:v4p427/r4.anchor: فهو يعلم أن ما قاله له أخوه من احتمال أو زاره حق

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r10.claim: The question may ask whether he knows the unseen and thus saw that what he heard was false.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r10.anchor: أعلم الغيب فرأى أن ما سمعه باطل

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r11.speaker: الكلبي
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r11.claim: Al-Kalbi takes it to mean revelation came to him, so he judged his conduct right.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r11.anchor: أنزل عليه القرآن فرأى ما صنعه حقا , قاله الكلبي

MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r12.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r12.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r12.claim: A further possibility is that he knew there is no resurrection and therefore expected no recompense.
MAWARDI-FULL:v5p402/r12.anchor: أعلم أن لا بعث , فهو يرى أن لا جزاء

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r1.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r1.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r1.claim: The sixth proposed aspect of the Quran's inimitability is its knowledge of the unseen and its truthful forecasts of future events.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r1.anchor: أن وجه إعجازه ، هو ما فيه من علم الغيب ، والإخبار بما يكون

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r2.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r2.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r2.claim: As evidence of foreknowledge, Jews were challenged to wish for death if the afterlife belonged exclusively to them, then told they would never wish for it because of their deeds; none did so.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r2.anchor: قل إن كانت لكم الدار الآخرة عند الله خالصة من دون الناس فتمنوا الموت إن كنتم صادقين

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r3.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r3.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r3.claim: The challenge to Quraysh predicted they would not produce a comparable surah, and they did not, another example of a fulfilled forecast.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r3.anchor: ^ ( فإن لم تفعلوا ولن تفعلوا ) ^ فقطع بأنهم لا يفعلون ، فلم يفعلوا

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r4.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r4.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r4.claim: A seventh aspect is that the Quran gathers knowledge beyond the capacities of the Arabs, their speech, or any scholar among other nations, and no other book contains it all.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r4.anchor: جامعا لعلوم لم تكن فيهم آلاتها ، ولا تتعاطى العرب الكلام فيها

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r5.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r5.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r5.claim: The claims that nothing is omitted from the Book and that it explains everything support the Quran's comprehensive knowledge.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r5.anchor: وقال تعالى : ^ ( ما فرطنا في الكتاب من شيء ) ^ وقال : ^ ( تبيانا لكل شيء ) ^

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r6.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r6.speaker: رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r6.claim: The Prophet describes the Quran as containing news of the past and reports of what comes after, as truth rather than jest, and says seeking guidance elsewhere leads astray; no grading is stated.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r6.anchor: وقال النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم : ' فيه خبر ما قبلكم ونبأ ما بعدكم هو الحق ليس بالهزل

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r7.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r7.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r7.claim: An eighth account locates the Quran's inimitability in sarfa: God turned their resolve away from answering the challenge to produce a surah like it.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r7.anchor: أن إعجازه هو الصرفة ، وهو أن الله تعالى صرف هممهم عن معارضته

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r8.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r8.speaker: القائلون بهذه الصرفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r8.claim: One sarfa view says people were stripped of the ability to compose a rival; even if they tried, they would fail.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r8.anchor: صرفوا عن القدرة عليه ، ولو تعرضوا لعجزوا عنه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r9.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r9.speaker: القائلون بهذه الصرفة
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r9.claim: The other sarfa view says people were diverted from attempting a rival despite having the ability, so they might have succeeded if they tried.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r9.anchor: صرفوا عن التعرض له ، مع كونه في قدرتهم ولو تعرضوا له لجاز أن يقدروا عليه

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r10.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r10.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r10.claim: Al-Mawardi concludes that all eight proposed aspects jointly make the Quran inimitable; none is uniquely preferable, and together they heighten its eloquence and concision.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r10.anchor: ليس اختصاص أحدها بأن يكون معجزا بأولى من غيره ، صار إعجازه من الأوجه الثمانية

MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r11.author: al-Māwardī
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r11.speaker: author
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r11.claim: Because of its inimitable form and meanings, Quranic wording needs careful, sustained reflection rather than reliance on first impressions; meanings may become clear or subtle at different times.
MAWARDI-FULL:v1p32/r11.anchor: احتاجت ألفاظه في استخراج معانيها إلى زيادة التأمل لها وفضل الروية فيها ، ولا يقتصر فيها على أوائل البديهة

MUQATIL:53:33-42/r3.author: Muqātil b. Sulaymān
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r3.speaker: author
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r3.claim: The question challenges whether he knows the unseen and sees that he will not be resurrected, thereby justifying persistence in disbelief; parallels are 52:41 and 68:47.
MUQATIL:53:33-42/r3.anchor: { أعنده علم الغيب } بأن الله لا يبعثه { فهو يرى } [آية: 35]

NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#4/r1.author: al-Nasafī
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#4/r1.speaker: author
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#4/r1.claim: Does the man know the unseen, so that he can see that the threat to bear Allah's punishment is true?
NASAFI-FULL:v4p191#4/r1.anchor: فهو يعلم ان ما ضمنه من عذاب الله حق

QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r6.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r6.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r6.claim: The question asks whether the miser knows unseen punishment and afterlife events, as if he could guarantee another's burden.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r6.anchor: أي أعند هذا المكدي علم ما غاب عنه من أمر العذاب؟

QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r7.author: al-Qurṭubī
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r7.speaker: author
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r7.claim: Raʾā is transitive to two omitted objects: he sees the unseen as plainly as the visible.
QURTUBI-FULL:53:34-35/r7.anchor: وهذه الرؤية هي المتعدية إلى مفعولين والمفعولان محذوفان

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r7.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r7.speaker: author
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r7.claim: The phrase asking whether he sees means asking whether he knows the truth of the matter.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r7.anchor: { فهو يرى } : فهو يعلم صحة ذلك

QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r8.author: al-Qushayrī
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r8.speaker: يقال
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r8.claim: One report identifies the person as a hypocrite who helps with jihad briefly and then stops, as if he knew his unseen afterlife state.
QUSHAYRI:v3p251/r8.anchor: يقال : هو المنافق الذي يعين على الجهاد قليلا ثم يقطع ذلك : { أعنده علم الغيب } : فهو يرى حاله في الآخرة

FARRA:v3p100/r4.author: al-Farrāʾ
FARRA:v3p100/r4.speaker: author
FARRA:v3p100/r4.claim: Farra reads this as a situation in the afterlife.
FARRA:v3p100/r4.anchor: «أعنده علم الغيب فهو يرى» (35) حالة في الآخرة
